outcomes.text: Explain how language choices shape meanings in texts.
Explain how different readers or listeners interpret texts.
Explain how texts relate to each other and to the contexts of their production and reception.
Explain how linguistic and literary approaches inform interpretations of texts.
Explain the significance of contextual factors in producing and receiving texts.
Apply linguistic and literary methods and concepts to support responses to texts.
Analyse texts at the level of phonetics, phonology and prosodics.
Analyse texts at the level of lexis and semantics.
Analyse texts at the level of grammar, including morphology.
Analyse texts at the level of pragmatics and discourse.
Explore connections between two texts, one from the anthology and one unseen.
Consider how the texts relate to each other and to the contexts in which they were produced and received.
Evaluate the effectiveness of texts for different audiences and purposes, drawing on wide reading and listening.
Analyse how language choices shape meanings.
Apply varied reading and listening strategies suited to text type and purpose.
Identify and describe how meanings and effects are created in non-fiction and spoken texts.
Identify linguistic methods such as phonology, lexis, semantics, grammar, morphology, pragmatics and discourse.
Apply linguistic methodologies and concepts to inform responses to and interpretations of texts.
Use English and terminology appropriately and coherently, with accurate reference to texts.

units.title: The language of poetry and plays

outcomes.text: Show knowledge and understanding of one substantial poetry collection chosen from six.
Analyse the use and impact of imagery, symbolism, rhythm, rhyme, tone, form and structure.
Analyse the use and impact of phonological, lexical, semantic and grammatical choices.
Analyse aspects foregrounded through repetition, pattern-making, pattern-breaking and deviation.
Explore connections across poems and how they relate to literary and other relevant contexts.
Identify and describe how meanings and effects are created through language, using terminology accurately.
Show knowledge and understanding of one drama text chosen from six.
Explore dramatic techniques: on-stage and off-stage action, paralinguistic features, soliloquy, asides and dramatic irony.
Analyse aspects foregrounded through repetition, pattern-making, pattern-breaking and deviation.
Identify and describe how meanings and effects are created through language.
Explore connections between a scene and the play as a whole, and the significance of dramatic, literary and generic contexts.

units.title: Reading as a writer, writing as a reader

outcomes.text: Show knowledge and understanding of one substantial prose fiction text chosen from six.
Show how literary and linguistic methods inform interpretations of the text.
Apply text analysis methods drawing on linguistic and literary techniques.
Identify how meanings and effects are created, and how language choices shape meaning.
Draw on generic and literary contexts to analyse a narrative text.
Produce an original narrative opening and a commentary on its techniques.
Show expertise and creativity in using English to communicate in different ways.
Apply analysis methods from linguistic and literary fields and describe how meanings and effects are created.

units.title: Independent study: analysing and producing texts

outcomes.text: Write a comparative analysis of a non-fiction text from a set list and a free-choice text, one published after 2000.
Apply text analysis methods drawing on linguistic and literary fields.
Identify and describe how meanings and effects are created and conveyed.
Make accurate reference to texts and sources.
Synthesise and reflect on knowledge of linguistic and literary concepts and methods.
Write an original non-fiction piece, such as travel writing, memoir, speech or digital text, with a short introduction on the techniques used.
Use techniques to produce and evaluate texts for different audiences and purposes, informed by wide reading.
Use English appropriately, accurately and creatively.
Reflect on linguistic and literary methods and how language choices shape meaning.
